2	#
3	# Controls where agents write generated artifacts, relative to the project root the
4	# pipeline is invoked from. Every agent reads this file first (see the "Output Location"
5	# section at the top of each prompt in prompts/) and falls back to these same defaults
6	# if this file is missing, so deleting it is safe — it just resets you to defaults.
7	
8	output_dir: output
9	runs_subdir: runs
10	run_id: null   # unset -> agents default to today's date (YYYY-MM-DD); set explicitly (e.g. a
11	               # release tag or CR number) to keep concurrent cycles cleanly separated
12	
13	# Optional inputs some agents look for. All may be left null and provided ad hoc by the user

15	inputs:
16	  requirements_docs: null    # path/glob to SRS/CR doc(s), read by requirements-analyzer
17	  logs_dir: null              # default directory log-analyzer looks in if none specified

21	# rename to match existing conventions without editing every agent prompt. All paths below

1	# Project Context
2	
3	Last updated: 2026-09-03 (run_id 2026-09-03) — Initial creation. No prior `context.md` existed in
4	`/hms/projects/m1_sdp/M1-SDP/m1-sdp-qa-pipeline` at time of writing; this document was built from
5	scratch by reading the codebase at `/hms/projects/m1_sdp/M1-SDP/m1-sdp` (HEAD detached at tag
6	`3.0.68`, latest commit `2b8c7f561`).
7	
8	## Overview
9	- **m1-sdp** (hSenid Mobile "M1 Service Delivery Platform") is a large, long-lived telecom SDP:
10	  it provisions and mediates value-added services (SMS, USSD, BAS/premium billing, WAP push, MMS)
11	  between mobile network operator gateways (SMSC/UCP, USSD GW, SS7/Sigtran, ECGS charging) and
12	  content/service providers, plus back-office apps for provisioning, charging config, and CDR
13	  reporting.
14	- Multi-module Maven reactor (`pom.xml`, `groupId hsenidmobile.sdp`, `artifactId m1-sdp`,
15	  currently version `3.0.68`) containing ~50 modules of very mixed vintage: modern Spring Boot 3
16	  apps sit alongside 2008-era Ant/Ivy webapps in the same repo.
17	- Confirmed from `README.md`: runtime is OpenJDK 21, MySQL 8.4.4, Maven 3+; legacy modules still
18	  build with Ant + `HSENID_BUILD_COMMON`/`CXF_HOME` env vars, and depend on external
19	  hSenid-internal connector projects (`ajuba-connector`, `ussd-connector`, `spml-connector`)
20	  built separately from their own repos.
21	
22	## Tech Stack
23	- **Languages/runtime:** Java 21 (`pom.xml` `maven.compiler.target=21`); a few legacy modules
24	  historically targeted Java 1.6 (`module.properties` in `core-logic`, `compile.target.version=1.6`,
25	  though the parent POM now forces 21 repo-wide).
26	- **Modern stack (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery):** Spring Boot 3.4.5, Spring
27	  6.2.6, Thymeleaf + Tailwind CSS, Spring Security OAuth2 Client (Keycloak SSO), Hibernate
28	  6.6.13, MySQL Connector/J 9.3.0, Log4j2 2.25.1, Jasper Reports/POI/iText (report-viewer-v2),
29	  Spring Data JPA (cdrquery).
30	- **Legacy stack (dashboard, provisioning, reportviewer, cdragent, etc.):** Ant + Ivy builds,
31	  JSP/Struts-style webapps, CAS-based SSO (`modules/cas`), c3p0 connection pooling, ehcache.
32	- **Messaging/integration middleware:** Mule ESB 3.x-style custom runtime
33	  (`modules/mule-integration`, packaged as `sdp-mule-integration`), RocksDB used as a local
34	  durable queue/burst buffer (`RocksDbBasedBurstServerEventHandler.java`, plus
35	  `RocksDbBurstHandler_FlowDiagram.md` at repo root documenting that flow).
36	- **DB:** MySQL, schema name `sdp_sla` (seen in `core-logic.properties`, `sbl-v2` README),
37	  accessed via JDBC/Hibernate/c3p0; `docker-compose.yaml` at root spins up `mysql:5.6.51` for
38	  local dev alongside newer modules that assume MySQL 8.4.4 — **version mismatch, not confirmed
39	  which is authoritative for current dev**.
40	- **Build tools present:** Maven (root `pom.xml`, `mvnw`), Ant (`build.xml` at root and in most
41	  legacy modules), Ivy (`ivy.xml` in legacy modules), npm/Tailwind (`package.json` in
42	  provisioning-v2 and report-viewer-v2 for CSS build only).
43	- **Auth:** Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC for the three new Spring Boot apps (see Architecture), CAS for
44	  legacy dashboard/provisioning/reportviewer apps.
45	
46	## Architecture
47	- Overall style: **service-oriented monolith-of-modules** — one Maven reactor, many
48	  independently deployable components communicating over HTTP(S), SMPP, and Mule-mediated
49	  queues, sharing one MySQL database (`sdp_sla`) as the source of truth for provisioning/SLA
50	  data.
51	- Confirmed request/message flow for SMS/USSD (from `modules/sbl-v2/README.md` and
52	  `docs/flow-testing`):
53	  ```
54	  SP/App --> SDP (core) --http/https:7000--> SBL-V2 --http/https:9966--> USSD GW
55	                          <--http/https:8888--
56	                SBL-V2 --smpp:3001/3002--> SMPP server(s)
57	  ```
58	  SBL-V2 = SMS/USSD load-balancing gateway component in front of the USSD GW and SMPP servers,
59	  with its own MySQL-backed SLA data and optional one-way TLS on both the SDP↔SBL-V2 and
60	  SBL-V2↔MySQL links.
61	- `modules/mule-integration` is the core MO/MT processing engine: routes messages through SBL
62	  (queue names in `sbl.properties`), UCP/number-checking (`numberchecking.properties`), ECGS
63	  charging (`charging.properties`), and NBL (`nbl.properties`); uses RocksDB-backed queues to
64	  survive bursts/restarts without losing in-flight messages.
65	- `modules/number-checking` performs subscriber/number-type lookups against MAP GW / Sigtran GW,
66	  with a caching layer and per-NCS-type (SMS vs BAS vs USSD) fallback-to-cache configuration
67	  (see `SMS_NUMBER_CHECKING_CONFIGURATION.md`).
68	- Three modern Spring Boot apps sit behind a single Apache HTTPD reverse proxy and one Keycloak
69	  realm for SSO (confirmed in `keycloak/KEYCLOAK_SSO_GUIDE.md`):
70	  ```
71	  Browser (HTTPS :443)
72	        -> Apache HTTPD
73	             /provisioning -> https://localhost:8082/provisioning  (provisioning-v2)
74	             /report       -> https://localhost:8084/report        (report-viewer-v2)
75	             /cdrquery     -> https://localhost:8088/cdrquery      (cdrquery)
76	             /             -> https://localhost:9443/              (Keycloak)
77	  ```
78	- `HAMultiHost_Flow_Diagram.md` documents a generic high-availability multi-host client
79	  (parses a comma-separated URL list, health-checks hosts, fails over) used for outbound
80	  connector calls — check which connectors use it before assuming any single one does; not
81	  independently confirmed which callers use `HAMultiHost` beyond the diagram doc.
82	
83	## Modules / Components
84	- **provisioning-v2** — Spring Boot 3 web app (Thymeleaf) for SP/application/CR provisioning
85	  and SLA management; Keycloak OAuth2 client, HTTPS on `:8082`, context path `/provisioning`.
86	  Path: `modules/provisioning-v2`
87	- **provisioning** (legacy) — original Ant/JSP provisioning webapp, CAS-secured, being
88	  superseded by provisioning-v2. Path: `modules/provisioning`
89	- **provisioning-startup-services** — shared startup/init services consumed by
90	  provisioning(-v2). Path: `modules/provisioning-startup-services`
91	- **dashboard** — legacy Ant/JSP operational dashboard (Flash-based charts under `flash_src/`),
92	  CAS-secured. Path: `modules/dashboard`
93	- **sbl-v2** — SMS/USSD load-balancing gateway in front of USSD GW/SMPP servers; Spring-based,
94	  MySQL-backed, optional mutual TLS. Path: `modules/sbl-v2`
95	- **mule-integration** — Mule-based core MO/MT message processing engine; RocksDB-backed burst
96	  queue; integrates SBL, number-checking/UCP, ECGS charging, NBL. Path: `modules/mule-integration`
97	- **number-checking** — subscriber number-type lookup/caching against MAP GW / Sigtran GW, with
98	  per-NCS-type (SMS/BAS/USSD) config. Path: `modules/number-checking`
99	- **charging** — charging/ECGS integration logic and its own DB setup scripts. Path:
100	  `modules/charging`
101	- **core-logic** (`sdp-core-logic`) — shared domain/business logic library (Hibernate entities,
102	  services) used by provisioning, provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, etc. Path: `core-logic`
103	- **component-integration** — integration glue module (legacy Ant/Ivy). Path:
104	  `modules/component-integration`
105	- **cas** — CAS server assets (`cas.zip`, JSPs) for legacy-app SSO. Path: `modules/cas`
106	- **cdragent / cdragent_v2** — CDR (call/message detail record) collection agent, legacy and v2.
107	  Path: `modules/cdragent`, `modules/cdragent_v2`
108	- **reporting/report-viewer-v2** — Spring Boot 3 reporting UI (JasperReports/POI/iText exports),
109	  Keycloak OAuth2, replacing legacy `reportviewer`. Path: `modules/reporting/report-viewer-v2`
110	- **reporting/cdrquery** — Spring Boot 3 app for CDR querying, Spring Data JPA + MySQL,
111	  OAuth2 client and resource-server (JWT) support, Keycloak-secured; has its own
112	  `KEYCLOAK-REALM-SETUP.md`. Path: `modules/reporting/cdrquery`
113	- **reporting/dataloader(_v2) / datarecover(_v2) / datatransfer(_v2)** — CDR/report data ETL
114	  utilities, legacy Ant and newer Maven variants coexist. Path: `modules/reporting/*`
115	- **traffic-controller** (`traffic-notification-client`, `traffic-updater`) — traffic
116	  control/notification components, Maven-based. Path: `modules/traffic-controller`
117	- **http-ha** — HTTP high-availability library (likely backs `HAMultiHost`). Path:
118	  `modules/http-ha`
119	- **web-core** (`sdp-web-core`) — shared web layer library used by several legacy/Boot apps.
120	  Path: `modules/web-core`
121	- **hms-common-ncs-message** — shared NCS (network/content service) message model library used
122	  across protocol-api connectors. Path: `modules/hms-common-ncs-message`
123	- **protocol-api/ussd, ecgs, sigtran-gw-connector, ucp** — protocol connector libraries for
124	  USSD, ECGS charging, SS7/Sigtran signalling, and UCP (SMSC protocol). Path: `protocol-api/*`
125	- **ws/{sms,bas,ussd,premium-service,sws,wap}/{skeleton,stub,async-resp}** — generated/handwritten
126	  SOAP web-service skeletons and client stubs per NCS channel (SMS, BAS, USSD, premium-service,
127	  SWS, WAP push). Path: `ws/*`
128	- **sdk/{sms,bas,ussd,sdp-https}/...** — sample SDK/reference client implementations per channel
129	  (e.g. `smsmania`, `douknw`, `mobigraphic-money-transfer`), used for integration testing against
130	  the ws skeletons. Path: `sdk/*`
131	- **simulators/** — protocol simulators for local/integration testing: `smpp-sim`, `ussd`
132	  (incl. `ussd-gw-jetty`, `core-simulator`, `ussd-genrator`), `ecgs`, `sigtran-gw`, `ucp`,
133	  `ajuba-sim`, `hms-ussd-sim`, `selenium-smpp-sim`, `sdp-ws`/`sdp-ws-4`, `ussd-sbl-mo`. Path:
134	  `simulators/*`
135	- **mock-servers** — WireMock + Python-based mocks (SMS delivery report mock, health/root
136	  mappings) for external HTTP dependencies, dockerized (`Dockerfile.wiremock`,
137	  `Dockerfile.python`, own `docker-compose.yml`). Path: `mock-servers/`
138	- **keycloak** — SSO/reverse-proxy setup guide and realm config references (no runtime code
139	  here beyond docs). Path: `keycloak/`
140	- **snmp / spam-filter / mobicents / subscription-nbl-app / migration / dbsetup / prs-db-migration /
141	  performance** — supporting modules for monitoring (SNMP traps), spam filtering, mobicents SS7
142	  stack integration, NBL subscriptions, DB migrations/setup scripts, and performance testing.
143	  Paths: `modules/snmp`, `modules/spam-filter`, `modules/mobicents`, `modules/subscription-nbl-app`,
144	  `modules/migration`, `modules/dbsetup`, `modules/prs-db-migration`, `modules/performance`
145	- **qa/** — pre-existing manual/legacy QA assets: Ant-built `provisioning-automated` test
146	  project, a large tree of ad-hoc `Automated_Scripts` (per-feature manual test scripts from past
147	  releases), and `grinder` load-test scripts/config (`m1sdpSMSMT.py`, etc.). Path: `qa/`
148	- **utils** — shared utility library (Maven). Path: `utils/`
149	
150	## Integration Points
151	- **HTTP(S) REST/SOAP** — provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery (REST/Thymeleaf); `ws/*`
152	  skeleton modules expose SOAP web services per channel (SMS/BAS/USSD/premium-service/SWS/WAP).
153	- **SMPP** — SBL-V2 talks to SMPP server(s) on configurable ports (example `3001`/`3002` in its
154	  README); `simulators/smpp-sim` and `simulators/selenium-smpp-sim` simulate this.
155	- **UCP (SMSC protocol)** — `protocol-api/ucp`, `simulators/ucp`; configured via
156	  `numberchecking.properties` in mule-integration.
157	- **USSD (HTTP-based USSD GW protocol)** — `protocol-api/ussd`, SBL-V2 → USSD GW on port
158	  `9966`/`8888` in the documented flow; `simulators/hms-ussd-sim`, `simulators/ussd/*`.
159	- **Sigtran / MAP GW (SS7 signalling)** — `protocol-api/sigtran-gw-connector`,
160	  `modules/mobicents`, `simulators/sigtran-gw`; used by number-checking for subscriber lookups.
161	- **ECGS (charging gateway)** — `protocol-api/ecgs`, `simulators/ecgs`; configured via
162	  `charging.properties`.
163	- **OAuth2/OIDC via Keycloak** — provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery all register as
164	  OAuth2 clients against a Keycloak realm (`provisioning-ui` realm shown in provisioning-v2's
165	  `application.yaml`); cdrquery additionally acts as an OAuth2 **resource server** (JWT
166	  validation) per its `spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server` dependency.
167	- **CAS SSO** — legacy dashboard/provisioning/reportviewer apps use `spring-security-cas`
168	  against the bundled `modules/cas` server.
169	- **MySQL** — shared `sdp_sla` schema for SLA/provisioning data (see `core-logic.properties`
170	  JDBC URL `jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:3306/sdp_sla`), plus separate schemas/scripts for reporting,
171	  dashboard, CDR query (`modules/dbsetup/conf/*`).
172	- **RocksDB** — embedded, used as a local durable burst/queue store in mule-integration (not a
173	  network integration point, but a real data-store dependency to know about for tests around
174	  restart/recovery behavior).
175	- **Mail (SMTP)** — provisioning-v2 depends on `spring-boot-starter-mail`
176	  (`emailMessageTemplate.properties`, `emailGroup.properties` present) — actual SMTP
177	  server/config not confirmed from code alone.
178	- **WireMock/mock HTTP servers** — `mock-servers/` mocks an SMS delivery-report HTTP endpoint
179	  for local/CI testing, not a production integration.
180	
181	## Test Conventions
182	- **Frameworks in use:** JUnit 4.12 (root `pom.xml` dependency, inherited by most Maven
183	  modules); JUnit 5 (Jupiter) + jmock-junit5 confirmed in `core-logic`, `modules/http-ha`,
184	  `modules/reporting/datarecover_v2`, `simulators/smpp-sim` — **the codebase mixes JUnit 4 and
185	  JUnit 5 across modules**, check per-module `pom.xml` before assuming which applies.
186	  `spring-boot-starter-test` (JUnit 5 + Mockito + AssertJ) is used in the three Spring Boot apps
187	  (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery) and `spring-security-test` in cdrquery.
188	- **Layout:** standard Maven `src/test/java` per module (56 modules have a `src/test` directory);
189	  legacy Ant modules (e.g. `qa/provisioning-automated`) use `src/test` + `src/dev` conventions
190	  under Ant/Ivy instead of Maven.
191	- **No CI pipeline file found in this repo** (`not confirmed`: no `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`,
192	  or `.github/workflows` present at the time of this scan) — build/test automation, if any, is
193	  likely orchestrated outside this repo or not yet checked in.
194	- **Running tests locally:** default is `mvn clean install` per module/reactor;
195	  README explicitly documents `mvn clean install -Dmaven.test.skip=true` as the standard build
196	  command, i.e. **tests are skipped by default in the documented build flow** — a QA agent should
197	  not assume `mvn install` alone exercises the test suite.
198	- **Local environment setup for manual/integration testing** (from README + module READMEs):
199	  - MySQL 8.4.4 (or `docker-compose.yaml`'s MySQL 5.6.51 for a lighter local DB — version
200	    mismatch, confirm which the team actually uses) with `sdp_sla` schema, seeded via
201	    `modules/dbsetup/conf/complete-install/readme.txt` and per-module sample dumps (e.g.
202	    `modules/mule-integration/conf/test/sample-db-dump.sql`).
203	  - External connector projects must be pre-built at pinned versions: `ajuba-connector`,
204	    `ussd-connector`, `spml-connector` (versions pinned in root `pom.xml`).
205	  - Protocol simulators under `simulators/*` and mocks under `mock-servers/` stand in for real
206	    network elements (SMPP, USSD GW, ECGS, Sigtran GW, SMS delivery reports) during local/manual
207	    testing — each has its own README.
208	  - Keycloak + self-signed TLS certs required to exercise provisioning-v2 / report-viewer-v2 /
209	    cdrquery end-to-end (see `keycloak/KEYCLOAK_SSO_GUIDE.md` and per-module
210	    `generate-ssl-cert.sh` / `KEYCLOAK-REALM-SETUP.md`).
211	- **Existing manual QA assets:** `qa/Automated_Scripts/*` — a large archive of historical,
212	  scenario-named manual test scripts (app creation, CR flow, MO/MT-only, WAP-only, etc.) from
213	  prior releases; `qa/grinder` — Jython load-test scripts for SMS/MMS/WAP-push MT flows.
214	
215	## Risk Notes
216	- **Mixed legacy/modern architecture** — Ant/Ivy/JSP/CAS modules (dashboard, provisioning,
217	  reportviewer, cdragent, most `protocol-api`/`ws`/`sdk` modules) coexist with new Spring Boot
218	  3 + Keycloak apps (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery). Migrations in progress
219	  ("v2" modules) mean **duplicate/parallel functionality** may exist (e.g. `provisioning` vs
220	  `provisioning-v2`, `reportviewer` vs `report-viewer-v2`) — confirm which is actually deployed
221	  before testing.
222	- **JDK/dependency upgrade churn** — recent commits (`git log`) show an active
223	  `jdk-upgrade/sdp-core` effort with jar-deduplication fixes ("Removed redundant jars with
224	  multiple versions: ehcache and hms-common-util", "Excluded duplicate BouncyCastle and unused
225	  spring-security-cas jars") — classpath/dependency-version regressions are a plausible recent
226	  risk area.
227	- **TLS/hostname-verification bugs in SBL-V2/USSD path** — recent fix commits
228	  (`ecf8d972f`, `6bfaaba1f`, and a revert `10e010bf9`) show SSL hostname verification and TLS
229	  version configuration for the ussd-connector was buggy enough that MO logs could silently show
230	  SUCCESS on a real SSL failure — this is a concrete, recently-touched fragile area worth
231	  regression testing around SBL-V2 TLS config.
232	- **RocksDB-backed burst queue in mule-integration** — recovery-on-restart logic
233	  (`RocksDbBasedBurstServerEventHandler`, documented in `RocksDbBurstHandler_FlowDiagram.md`,
234	  plus a 44 KB `RocksDB_Performance_Investigation.md` at repo root) indicates this area has had
235	  real performance/correctness investigations — treat message durability/ordering across
236	  restarts as a fragile area.
237	- **Shared single MySQL schema (`sdp_sla`)** across many modules (provisioning-v2, sbl-v2,
238	  mule-integration, etc.) — schema changes in one module's DB setup scripts can affect others;
239	  no evidence of per-module schema isolation.
240	- **Auth boundary duality** — CAS (legacy) vs Keycloak/OAuth2 (new apps) means session/SSO
241	  behavior differs by app; cdrquery is also a JWT resource server, widening its auth surface
242	  (token validation bugs would be distinct from the cookie-based apps).
243	- **Hardcoded example secrets/passwords in checked-in config** — e.g. plaintext DB password
244	  (`jdbc.password=password`), Keycloak client secret, and keystore passwords in
245	  `provisioning-v2/src/main/resources/application.yaml` and `core-logic.properties` — likely
246	  dev-only defaults, but flag for review; not confirmed whether production overrides these via
247	  externalized config.
248	- **External/pinned connector dependencies** (`ajuba-connector`, `ussd-connector`,
249	  `spml-connector`) live in separate repos and must be built at exact pinned versions — version
250	  drift here is a build/integration risk outside this repo's direct control.
251	- **No CI pipeline definition found in-repo** — regression safety net (if any) is not visible
252	  from the codebase itself; cannot confirm what, if anything, runs automatically on commits/PRs.
253	
254	## Not Confirmed
255	- Whether any CI/CD pipeline (Jenkins, GitLab CI, etc.) actually runs against this repo — no
256	  pipeline definition file found in the working tree.
257	- Which MySQL version is authoritative for local dev — root `docker-compose.yaml` provisions
258	  `mysql:5.6.51` while README and several module READMEs (sbl-v2, mule-integration) specify
259	  MySQL 8.4.4.
260	- Whether `provisioning`/`dashboard`/`reportviewer` (legacy, CAS-based) are still actively
261	  deployed in production alongside their "v2" Spring Boot replacements, or fully retired.
262	- Actual production values for Keycloak realm/client config, SMTP server, and SNMP trap
263	  destinations — only dev/example values were found in checked-in `application.yaml` /
264	  `*.properties` files.
265	- Precise meaning of some project-specific acronyms (NCS, NBL, SWS, BAS) beyond what's inferable
266	  from config/package names — no glossary found in the repo; inferred from context (NCS ≈
267	  "network/content service" channel type such as SMS/BAS/USSD; BAS ≈ premium billing/bearer
268	  application service based on `sdk/bas`, `ws/bas` content) but not explicitly defined anywhere
269	  read.
270	- Full behavior/ownership of the `patch/`, `mule-patch/`, `native-binary/`, and `support/`
271	  top-level directories — appear to be historical patch sets and native library overrides but
272	  were not deeply inspected.

- **m1-sdp** (hSenid Mobile "M1 Service Delivery Platform") is a large, long-lived telecom SDP:
  it provisions and mediates value-added services (SMS, USSD, BAS/premium billing, WAP push, MMS)
  between mobile network operator gateways (SMSC/UCP, USSD GW, SS7/Sigtran, ECGS charging) and
  content/service providers, plus back-office apps for provisioning, charging config, and CDR
  reporting.
- Multi-module Maven reactor (`pom.xml`, `groupId hsenidmobile.sdp`, `artifactId m1-sdp`,
  currently version `3.0.68`) containing ~50 modules of very mixed vintage: modern Spring Boot 3
  apps sit alongside 2008-era Ant/Ivy webapps in the same repo.
- Confirmed from `README.md`: runtime is OpenJDK 21, MySQL 8.4.4, Maven 3+; legacy modules still
  build with Ant + `HSENID_BUILD_COMMON`/`CXF_HOME` env vars, and depend on external
  hSenid-internal connector projects (`ajuba-connector`, `ussd-connector`, `spml-connector`)
  built separately from their own repos.

## Tech Stack
- **Languages/runtime:** Java 21 (`pom.xml` `maven.compiler.target=21`); a few legacy modules
  historically targeted Java 1.6 (`module.properties` in `core-logic`, `compile.target.version=1.6`,
  though the parent POM now forces 21 repo-wide).
- **Modern stack (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery):** Spring Boot 3.4.5, Spring
  6.2.6, Thymeleaf + Tailwind CSS, Spring Security OAuth2 Client (Keycloak SSO), Hibernate
  6.6.13, MySQL Connector/J 9.3.0, Log4j2 2.25.1, Jasper Reports/POI/iText (report-viewer-v2),
  Spring Data JPA (cdrquery).
- **Legacy stack (dashboard, provisioning, reportviewer, cdragent, etc.):** Ant + Ivy builds,
  JSP/Struts-style webapps, CAS-based SSO (`modules/cas`), c3p0 connection pooling, ehcache.
- **Messaging/integration middleware:** Mule ESB 3.x-style custom runtime
  (`modules/mule-integration`, packaged as `sdp-mule-integration`), RocksDB used as a local
  durable queue/burst buffer (`RocksDbBasedBurstServerEventHandler.java`, plus
  `RocksDbBurstHandler_FlowDiagram.md` at repo root documenting that flow).
- **DB:** MySQL, schema name `sdp_sla` (seen in `core-logic.properties`, `sbl-v2` README),
  accessed via JDBC/Hibernate/c3p0; `docker-compose.yaml` at root spins up `mysql:5.6.51` for
  local dev alongside newer modules that assume MySQL 8.4.4 — **version mismatch, not confirmed
  which is authoritative for current dev**.
- **Build tools present:** Maven (root `pom.xml`, `mvnw`), Ant (`build.xml` at root and in most
  legacy modules), Ivy (`ivy.xml` in legacy modules), npm/Tailwind (`package.json` in
  provisioning-v2 and report-viewer-v2 for CSS build only).
- **Auth:** Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC for the three new Spring Boot apps (see Architecture), CAS for
  legacy dashboard/provisioning/reportviewer apps.

## Architecture
- Overall style: **service-oriented monolith-of-modules** — one Maven reactor, many
  independently deployable components communicating over HTTP(S), SMPP, and Mule-mediated
  queues, sharing one MySQL database (`sdp_sla`) as the source of truth for provisioning/SLA
  data.
- Confirmed request/message flow for SMS/USSD (from `modules/sbl-v2/README.md` and
  `docs/flow-testing`):
  ```
  SP/App --> SDP (core) --http/https:7000--> SBL-V2 --http/https:9966--> USSD GW
                          <--http/https:8888--
                SBL-V2 --smpp:3001/3002--> SMPP server(s)
  ```
  SBL-V2 = SMS/USSD load-balancing gateway component in front of the USSD GW and SMPP servers,
  with its own MySQL-backed SLA data and optional one-way TLS on both the SDP↔SBL-V2 and
  SBL-V2↔MySQL links.
- `modules/mule-integration` is the core MO/MT processing engine: routes messages through SBL
  (queue names in `sbl.properties`), UCP/number-checking (`numberchecking.properties`), ECGS
  charging (`charging.properties`), and NBL (`nbl.properties`); uses RocksDB-backed queues to
  survive bursts/restarts without losing in-flight messages.
- `modules/number-checking` performs subscriber/number-type lookups against MAP GW / Sigtran GW,
  with a caching layer and per-NCS-type (SMS vs BAS vs USSD) fallback-to-cache configuration
  (see `SMS_NUMBER_CHECKING_CONFIGURATION.md`).
- Three modern Spring Boot apps sit behind a single Apache HTTPD reverse proxy and one Keycloak
  realm for SSO (confirmed in `keycloak/KEYCLOAK_SSO_GUIDE.md`):
  ```
  Browser (HTTPS :443)
        -> Apache HTTPD
             /provisioning -> https://localhost:8082/provisioning  (provisioning-v2)
             /report       -> https://localhost:8084/report        (report-viewer-v2)
             /cdrquery     -> https://localhost:8088/cdrquery      (cdrquery)
             /             -> https://localhost:9443/              (Keycloak)
  ```
- `HAMultiHost_Flow_Diagram.md` documents a generic high-availability multi-host client
  (parses a comma-separated URL list, health-checks hosts, fails over) used for outbound
  connector calls — check which connectors use it before assuming any single one does; not
  independently confirmed which callers use `HAMultiHost` beyond the diagram doc.

## Integration Points

- **UCP (SMSC protocol)** — `protocol-api/ucp`, `simulators/ucp`; configured via
  `numberchecking.properties` in mule-integration.
- **USSD (HTTP-based USSD GW protocol)** — `protocol-api/ussd`, SBL-V2 → USSD GW on port
  `9966`/`8888` in the documented flow; `simulators/hms-ussd-sim`, `simulators/ussd/*`.
- **Sigtran / MAP GW (SS7 signalling)** — `protocol-api/sigtran-gw-connector`,
  `modules/mobicents`, `simulators/sigtran-gw`; used by number-checking for subscriber lookups.
- **ECGS (charging gateway)** — `protocol-api/ecgs`, `simulators/ecgs`; configured via
  `charging.properties`.
- **OAuth2/OIDC via Keycloak** — provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery all register as
  OAuth2 clients against a Keycloak realm (`provisioning-ui` realm shown in provisioning-v2's

  dashboard, CDR query (`modules/dbsetup/conf/*`).
- **RocksDB** — embedded, used as a local durable burst/queue store in mule-integration (not a
  network integration point, but a real data-store dependency to know about for tests around

  server/config not confirmed from code alone.
- **WireMock/mock HTTP servers** — `mock-servers/` mocks an SMS delivery-report HTTP endpoint
  for local/CI testing, not a production integration.

## Test Conventions
- **Frameworks in use:** JUnit 4.12 (root `pom.xml` dependency, inherited by most Maven
  modules); JUnit 5 (Jupiter) + jmock-junit5 confirmed in `core-logic`, `modules/http-ha`,
  `modules/reporting/datarecover_v2`, `simulators/smpp-sim` — **the codebase mixes JUnit 4 and
  JUnit 5 across modules**, check per-module `pom.xml` before assuming which applies.
  `spring-boot-starter-test` (JUnit 5 + Mockito + AssertJ) is used in the three Spring Boot apps
  (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery) and `spring-security-test` in cdrquery.
- **Layout:** standard Maven `src/test/java` per module (56 modules have a `src/test` directory);
  legacy Ant modules (e.g. `qa/provisioning-automated`) use `src/test` + `src/dev` conventions
  under Ant/Ivy instead of Maven.
- **No CI pipeline file found in this repo** (`not confirmed`: no `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`,
  or `.github/workflows` present at the time of this scan) — build/test automation, if any, is
  likely orchestrated outside this repo or not yet checked in.
- **Running tests locally:** default is `mvn clean install` per module/reactor;
  README explicitly documents `mvn clean install -Dmaven.test.skip=true` as the standard build
  command, i.e. **tests are skipped by default in the documented build flow** — a QA agent should
  not assume `mvn install` alone exercises the test suite.
- **Local environment setup for manual/integration testing** (from README + module READMEs):
  - MySQL 8.4.4 (or `docker-compose.yaml`'s MySQL 5.6.51 for a lighter local DB — version
    mismatch, confirm which the team actually uses) with `sdp_sla` schema, seeded via
    `modules/dbsetup/conf/complete-install/readme.txt` and per-module sample dumps (e.g.
    `modules/mule-integration/conf/test/sample-db-dump.sql`).
  - External connector projects must be pre-built at pinned versions: `ajuba-connector`,
    `ussd-connector`, `spml-connector` (versions pinned in root `pom.xml`).
  - Protocol simulators under `simulators/*` and mocks under `mock-servers/` stand in for real
    network elements (SMPP, USSD GW, ECGS, Sigtran GW, SMS delivery reports) during local/manual
    testing — each has its own README.
  - Keycloak + self-signed TLS certs required to exercise provisioning-v2 / report-viewer-v2 /
    cdrquery end-to-end (see `keycloak/KEYCLOAK_SSO_GUIDE.md` and per-module
    `generate-ssl-cert.sh` / `KEYCLOAK-REALM-SETUP.md`).
- **Existing manual QA assets:** `qa/Automated_Scripts/*` — a large archive of historical,
  scenario-named manual test scripts (app creation, CR flow, MO/MT-only, WAP-only, etc.) from
  prior releases; `qa/grinder` — Jython load-test scripts for SMS/MMS/WAP-push MT flows.

## Risk Notes
- **Mixed legacy/modern architecture** — Ant/Ivy/JSP/CAS modules (dashboard, provisioning,
  reportviewer, cdragent, most `protocol-api`/`ws`/`sdk` modules) coexist with new Spring Boot
  3 + Keycloak apps (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery). Migrations in progress
  ("v2" modules) mean **duplicate/parallel functionality** may exist (e.g. `provisioning` vs
  `provisioning-v2`, `reportviewer` vs `report-viewer-v2`) — confirm which is actually deployed
  before testing.
- **JDK/dependency upgrade churn** — recent commits (`git log`) show an active
  `jdk-upgrade/sdp-core` effort with jar-deduplication fixes ("Removed redundant jars with
  multiple versions: ehcache and hms-common-util", "Excluded duplicate BouncyCastle and unused
  spring-security-cas jars") — classpath/dependency-version regressions are a plausible recent
  risk area.
- **TLS/hostname-verification bugs in SBL-V2/USSD path** — recent fix commits
  (`ecf8d972f`, `6bfaaba1f`, and a revert `10e010bf9`) show SSL hostname verification and TLS
  version configuration for the ussd-connector was buggy enough that MO logs could silently show
  SUCCESS on a real SSL failure — this is a concrete, recently-touched fragile area worth
  regression testing around SBL-V2 TLS config.
- **RocksDB-backed burst queue in mule-integration** — recovery-on-restart logic
  (`RocksDbBasedBurstServerEventHandler`, documented in `RocksDbBurstHandler_FlowDiagram.md`,
  plus a 44 KB `RocksDB_Performance_Investigation.md` at repo root) indicates this area has had
  real performance/correctness investigations — treat message durability/ordering across
  restarts as a fragile area.
- **Shared single MySQL schema (`sdp_sla`)** across many modules (provisioning-v2, sbl-v2,
  mule-integration, etc.) — schema changes in one module's DB setup scripts can affect others;
  no evidence of per-module schema isolation.
- **Auth boundary duality** — CAS (legacy) vs Keycloak/OAuth2 (new apps) means session/SSO
  behavior differs by app; cdrquery is also a JWT resource server, widening its auth surface
  (token validation bugs would be distinct from the cookie-based apps).
- **Hardcoded example secrets/passwords in checked-in config** — e.g. plaintext DB password
  (`jdbc.password=password`), Keycloak client secret, and keystore passwords in
  `provisioning-v2/src/main/resources/application.yaml` and `core-logic.properties` — likely
  dev-only defaults, but flag for review; not confirmed whether production overrides these via
  externalized config.
- **External/pinned connector dependencies** (`ajuba-connector`, `ussd-connector`,
  `spml-connector`) live in separate repos and must be built at exact pinned versions — version
  drift here is a build/integration risk outside this repo's direct control.
- **No CI pipeline definition found in-repo** — regression safety net (if any) is not visible
  from the codebase itself; cannot confirm what, if anything, runs automatically on commits/PRs.

## Not Confirmed
- Whether any CI/CD pipeline (Jenkins, GitLab CI, etc.) actually runs against this repo — no
  pipeline definition file found in the working tree.
- Which MySQL version is authoritative for local dev — root `docker-compose.yaml` provisions
  `mysql:5.6.51` while README and several module READMEs (sbl-v2, mule-integration) specify
  MySQL 8.4.4.
- Whether `provisioning`/`dashboard`/`reportviewer` (legacy, CAS-based) are still actively
  deployed in production alongside their "v2" Spring Boot replacements, or fully retired.
- Actual production values for Keycloak realm/client config, SMTP server, and SNMP trap
  destinations — only dev/example values were found in checked-in `application.yaml` /
  `*.properties` files.
- Precise meaning of some project-specific acronyms (NCS, NBL, SWS, BAS) beyond what's inferable
  from config/package names — no glossary found in the repo; inferred from context (NCS ≈
  "network/content service" channel type such as SMS/BAS/USSD; BAS ≈ premium billing/bearer
  application service based on `sdk/bas`, `ws/bas` content) but not explicitly defined anywhere
  read.
- Full behavior/ownership of the `patch/`, `mule-patch/`, `native-binary/`, and `support/`
  top-level directories — appear to be historical patch sets and native library overrides but
  were not deeply inspected.

  `SpRepositoryImpl`) and the `ApplicationListBySpUserService`/`BaseProvisioningService` were
  restructured to support it, replacing the old `AppListService`. Affected: `provisioning-v2`

  support (`ussd-connector.ssl.hostname-verification-enabled`,
  `ussd-connector.ssl.enabled-protocols`) so SBL-v2's USSD connector client can enforce hostname
  verification and pin allowed TLS versions (defaults to `TLSv1.3,TLSv1.2`); bumped
  `ussd-connector` dependency 1.0.86 → 1.0.89. Affected: `sbl-v2`
  (`modules/sbl-v2/src/main/java/com/hms/sbl/v2/configuration/Configuration.java`,
  `application.yaml`), `pom.xml`. Ref: `ecf8d972f`, `10e010bf9`

  instead of ad-hoc per-controller handling. Affected: `reporting/report-viewer-v2`
  (`v2/controller/*`). Ref: `ce807dfda`

  DB-connectivity error-handling logic out of ~19 individual report controllers

  `reporting/report-viewer-v2` / `reporting/datatransfer_v2` (`DatabaseConfig.java`, report
  controllers). Ref: `917aa5c3e`

  Affected: `reporting/report-viewer-v2`. Ref: `a0f4927ca`
